name: tui-router
tagline: Every part of the router on one screen
description:
The read-only cockpit for a Linux router. One screen, one card per area — interfaces and their WAN/LAN roles, the firewall's posture, live traffic per interface, the DHCP server and its leases, the WireGuard peers — read from cheap system probes and refreshed in place.

It changes nothing itself. Press ENTER on a card and tui-router suspends, hands the terminal to the tool that manages that area — tui-firewall, tui-network, tui-traffic, tui-vpn — and resumes when you leave it, the same handoff the family launcher uses. The overview is here; the change happens in the tool the card opens, behind that tool's own preview and confirm.

screenshots.caption: The cockpit: one card per area of the router, refreshed in place

keys.action: Open the tool that manages the selected card

notes.impact: `ip -j` (JSON output) is missing, so the interface and route cards cannot be read from this version

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-router
cd tui-router && make demo
source.note: Or run it against a sample router with `tui-router --demo`, which needs nothing installed.

pacman.note: Available once tui-router's first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

apt.note: Available once tui-router's first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

dnf.note: Available once tui-router's first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-router/releases/download/v{version}/tui-router_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-router
sudo install -m0755 tui-router /usr/local/bin/tui-router

security.needs_sudo: The cockpit only reads. Most reads are unprivileged; the ones that need root (the nftables ruleset, `ufw status`, the WireGuard dump) escalate with `sudo -n`, which never prompts, and a card that cannot escalate reads unknown. Nothing here changes the machine.
